newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran urges U.N. role to end Afghan fighting.
newsitem.headline: Iran urges U.N. role to end Afghan fighting.

text.p: Iran has called on the United Nations to intervene politically in Afghanistan and prepare the ground for reconciliation in the war-ravaged country, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Thursday.
It said the call was made by Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati in a letter to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

"This bleak situation requires your immediate attention and political intervention, including through exertion of pressure on war mongering factions and their foreign supporters, to prepare the grounds for national reconciliation and lasting peace in this war-torn country," it quoted the letter as saying.

Velayati attacked foreign intervention in neighbouring Afghanistan -- an apparent reference to Pakistan which Iran accuses of aiding the Islamic Taleban -- and warned that Iran viewed "the situation with grave concern and considers it a serious threat to peace and security in the region."

He said "the Afghan crisis eludes a military solution, and policies and practices bent on suppression, intimidation and violation of the most basic human rights do not but deepen the crisis and further exacerbate the situation in that country."
Shi'ite Moslem Iran supported the previous Kabul government ousted by the Sunni Taleban, which it accused of giving Islam a bad name by its harsh interpretation of Islamic law.

Taleban strengthened its claim to be the government of Afghanistan when it seized territory held by a rival group in the north of the country although it lost control on Wednesday of the key city of Mazar-i-Sharif, dealing the Islamic militia one of its worst setbacks since it seized Kabul in September.
Pakistan, which denies aiding the Taleban, has recognised the group, but Iran said it was not yet ready to recognise the Taleban.
